paragraphs: (Asa king of Judah, I Kings, supplied locator פו"ו-ח.) He is mentioned in Bamidbar Rabbah 6:10; Hyman says the reading should undoubtedly be R' Assi.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Midrash Rabbah — TE digital text of Bamidbar Rabbah 6:10 writes Rabbi Asa, agreeing with the supplied name. Assi is Hyman’s conjecture, expressed with “undoubtedly.” The royal introduction’s compressed biblical locator was previously interpreted contextually as I Kings 15:8, not as a demonstrated recovery of every supplied letter.

The whole Torat Emet Bamidbar Rabbah 6:10 paragraph fully writes Rabbi Asa, supporting that heading. It does not establish a full Rabbi title for Hyman’s conjectural Assi, rendered R'; ‘undoubtedly should read’ remains his judgment. The whole I Kings 15:8 verse names Asa succeeding Abijam, a positive contextual comparison only. The malformed supplied פו״ו–ח locator is now visible in the translation; the retained note’s contextual 15:8 interpretation does not establish a recovery of its letters or identify the sage with the king.
